Article Title: Apple touches $5 trillion market cap and one of the reasons is what has made Wall Street ‘unhappy’ with Google, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon
Article Text:
Why Alphabet’s capex hike changed how investors read AI spending across Big Tech



How Apple’s rented AI infrastructure keeps its cash flow intact while rivals borrow



Apple shares hit $342.89 on Tuesday, briefly putting the company’s market value at $5.036 trillion. That makes it the second company ever to reach $5 trillion, after Nvidia. The stock closed at $340.08, so the milestone lasted only part of the session. On Monday, Apple had already passed Nvidia to become the world’s most valuable public company again.Apple’s capital expenditure in fiscal 2025 was $12.7 billion. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta will spend more than $700 billion between them this year, nearly all of it on AI data centres. Twelve months ago that gap was Apple’s biggest problem on Wall Street. It is now the reason investors are buying the stock, and the shift happened almost entirely in the last week.Alphabet raised the top end of its 2026 capex forecast to $205 billion from $190 billion last Wednesday. Its cloud business grew 82% in the quarter, the fastest since at least 2020. The stock still fell 7% the next day, and took Amazon, Meta and Microsoft down with it.What spooked investors was the debt. Alphabet’s long-term borrowings have risen 111% to $98 billion in six months, and the company posted negative free cash flow last quarter for the first time.Amazon’s long-term debt climbed 81% to $119 billion between December and March. FactSet’s analysts now expect Microsoft’s free cash flow to turn negative in the fourth quarter, which would be a first since at least 2001.Apple buys compute rather than building it. CFO Kevan Parekh has called it a hybrid model, mixing first and third-party capacity, with Apple silicon running the servers it does own. The Siri overhaul due this fall leans on Google’s AI technology.The result showed up in March: over $28 billion in operating cash flow, capex under $3 billion, almost all of it free cash. “Once criticized for not spending more on AI, they have been able to avoid some of those capex pitfalls,” said Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets. Apple is up about 25% this year. Nvidia, which crossed $5 trillion in October, has managed 6%.Microsoft and Meta report Wednesday after the close, Amazon on Thursday. All three are expected to raise spending guidance. Cowen analyst Derrick Wood said another increase would probably trigger more selling.Apple reports Thursday evening, with analysts forecasting revenue growth above 15%. It will be Tim Cook’s last earnings call. John Ternus takes over on September 1.
Article Summary: Apple shares hit $342.89 on Tuesday, briefly putting the company’s market value at $5.036 trillion. That makes it the second company ever to reach $5 trillion, after Nvidia. Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta will spend more than $700 billion between them this year.

Article Title: US government continues ban on Chinese technology, now bans the gadgets that Elon Musk once said are Tesla's biggest competition
Article Text:
During Tesla earnings call, Elon Musk said “I think China will be by far the biggest competitor in the humanoid robot market" (Representative image)

What US government said on banning China’s humanoid robots

When Elon Musk called China’s humanoid robots as Tesla’s biggest long-term competition





The US Federal Communications Commission has banned humanoid robots from China citing "unacceptable risks” to national security. The Trump administration identified human robots as advanced robotic devices that include four-legged quadrupeds, bipeds, and wheeled and tracked vehicles. The move comes as the US government continues to tighten its control on Chinese technology across sectors ranging from telecommunications and drones to artificial intelligence to now humanoid robots. Notably, Elon Musk has previously described China’s humanoid robots as Tesla’s biggest long-term competition.In its determination of the threats posed by robots, FCC said:“As the technology matures, advanced robotic devices have growing use cases in monitoring and securing critical infrastructure. Robots are often equipped with high-fidelity sensors, including Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), tactile, acoustic, and thermal sensors that collect and maintain sensitive data on their surroundings”.“In addition to securing critical infrastructure, advanced robotic devices also have applications in industrial manufacturing, from material handling to order fulfilment. Integrating these technologies into American manufacturing will lower production costs, increase output, and support America’s reindustrialization.In order for the American economy to rely on these technologies, we must have a secure domestic advanced robotics supply chain and industrial Base,” it further stated.Adding further, the FCC said:“All foreign-produced advanced robotic devices pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States and to the safety and security of U.S. persons and should be included on the FCC’s Covered List, unless the Department of War (DOW) transmits to the FCC a specific determination that a given foreign-produced advanced robotic device, or a class of such devices, does not pose such risks”.Speaking at the company’s earnings call recently, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said that the electric vehicle maker’s future is increasingly tied to Optimus, humanoid robot program. "My prediction is that Optimus will be the biggest product of all time by far," Elon Musk said on the call. "Nothing will even be close. I think it'll be ten times bigger than the next biggest product ever made. That level," he added.During the earnings, he also acknowledged that Tesla is unlikely to dominate it alone. “I think China will be by far the biggest competitor in the humanoid robot market,” he said adding “China is extremely good at scaling and manufacturing, and is also strong in AI — the models being released there are already quite good and are improving rapidly.”“China's very good at AI, very good at manufacturing, and will definitely be the toughest competition for Tesla,” Elon Musk said, adding “To the best of our knowledge, we don't see any significant competitors outside of China, but China will definitely be tough competition, there's no two ways about it.”
Article Summary: The US Federal Communications Commission has banned humanoid robots from China citing ‘unacceptable risks’ to national security. The move comes as the US government continues to tighten its control on Chinese technology across sectors ranging from telecommunications and drones to artificial intelligence. Notably, Elon Musk has previously described China’s humanoid robots as Tesla's biggest long-term competition.

Article Title: Can ICE or CBP read your deleted messages: Here's what US Customs and Border Protection can and cannot do with your electronic devices at airports
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

“Can ICE or CBP read your deleted messages? The answer is yes,”

What CBP can do with electronic devices at airports



Basic search: Officers may review information stored on a device without requiring reasonable suspicion.

Advanced search: Officers may connect external equipment to copy or analyse a device's contents, but only when there is reasonable suspicion of a violation of laws enforced by CBP or a national security concern. Advanced searches also require supervisory approval.

What CBP cannot do during a border search



Can CBP recover deleted messages



ICE and CBP follow different policies



A recent Instagram video by immigration attorney Deepak Ahluwalia has raised questions about whether US border officials can recover deleted messages from travellers' phones during airport inspections. In the video, Ahluwalia claims that a client entering the US through San Francisco International Airport had permanently deleted messages that were recovered and reviewed during an inspection by US Customs and Border Protection (CBP).Ahluwalia said in the video. He added that, according to the client, CBP officers recovered messages that were not linked to any cloud service and had been permanently deleted, and that those messages were later used in deciding the individual's entry into the US. However, CBP's policy does not specifically state whether deleted messages can be recovered during a border search, but it does outline what officers are permitted and not permitted to do when examining electronic devices.Under CBP's Border Search of Electronic Devices directive, officers may inspect electronic devices, including mobile phones, tablets, laptops, smartwatches, cameras, and storage devices, as part of border inspections conducted when people enter or leave the US. The searches are intended to support customs, immigration, law enforcement and homeland security responsibilities. The directive allows officers to conduct two types of searches:CBP may also request that travellers unlock their devices or provide passcodes to facilitate an inspection.If officers cannot inspect a passcode-protected or encrypted device, they may detain it while determining how to proceed.The directive also places limits on electronic device searches. According to the policy, officers may not intentionally access information stored solely remotely, such as data stored only in cloud storage. To avoid accessing remote information, officers are instructed to ask travellers to place devices in airplane mode and disable Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, or disable network connectivity themselves when necessary.The directive further states that passcodes obtained during an inspection may be used only to inspect the device and the information stored on it. They cannot be used to access information that exists only remotely, and any recorded passcodes should be deleted or destroyed once they are no longer needed for the search.CBP's directive does not specifically address whether officers can recover permanently deleted messages from electronic devices or whether forensic tools may be used to do so.However, the policy permits advanced searches involving external equipment to analyse device contents when legal requirements are met, and it also allows CBP to seek technical assistance if a device is encrypted or otherwise not readily accessible.Because the directive does not explicitly discuss deleted messages, it does not confirm or deny whether such information can be recovered during a border inspection.The directive also notes that it applies to searches conducted by CBP. Searches performed by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), including Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), are governed by ICE's own policies and procedures. If CBP transfers a device or copied information to HSI for further analysis, ICE policies apply after HSI receives the device or information.
Article Summary: US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) searches electronic devices at airports. CBP's policy does not specifically state whether deleted messages can be recovered during a border search, but it does outline what officers are permitted and not permitted to do when examining electronic devices.

Article Title: What made California's largest AI datacenter that had promised not to use Colorado River water to file lawsuit to access 280 million gallons of river water meant for farming
Article Text:
Company says wastewater rejection forced change in plans

Why California’s largest AI data centre is opposed

California's largest planned AI data centre has filed a lawsuit to gain access to Colorado River water after its original plan to use recycled wastewater for cooling fell through. According to a report by Business Insider, the lawsuit has been filed by Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing which says that it needs around 287 million gallons of water a year to cool its proposed 330-megawatt facility, which would be the biggest AI data centre in the state. The company had earlier promised not to use Colorado River water because it expected to receive treated wastewater from nearby cities. But after two cities rejected its request, the company is now seeking access to river water, raising concerns about its impact on farming in the region.The proposed data centre in California is said to be the state’s largest data centre. It was originally designed to use reclaimed wastewater supplied by the cities of El Centro and Imperial. However, both cities declined to provide the water for cooling. The Imperial Irrigation District (IID), which manages Colorado River water in the region, also rejected the company's request.Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing has now filed a lawsuit seeking access to the water.The company is now asking for about 287 million gallons of water a year, or roughly 750,000 gallons a day.Although that amounts to only 0.028% of the IID's annual Colorado River allocation, the request has sparked opposition because of where the water would come from.The Colorado River supplies water to about 40 million people across seven western US states and is the only source of fresh water for around 180,000 people in Imperial Valley. Agriculture uses around 80% of California's Colorado River allocation, while 95% to 97% of the water distributed by the IID goes to farms.According to the company, the project would not require additional water from the river. Instead, it plans to buy nearby farmland along with its existing water rights and transfer those allocations to the data centre after farming on the land stops.Project lawyer Sebastian Rucci said the facility's water use would be similar to that of a 160-acre farm and would not increase pressure on the Colorado River. However, water experts say the issue is not the amount of water the project needs but the long-term impact of converting farmland into industrial land."There's a lot of resistance in any agricultural community to 'buy and dry' because that's jobs," a senior fellow at the Pacific Institute told Business Insider.Experts warned that while landowners may benefit from selling farmland and water rights, surrounding communities could lose jobs not only on farms but also in businesses that support agriculture, including equipment suppliers, repair shops and fertiliser sellers.The company says the project would create 1,688 construction jobs, more than 100 permanent jobs, and generate an estimated $2.95 billion in economic impact over 30 years. However, critics question whether those permanent jobs would make up for the potential loss of hundreds, or even thousands, of farming and agriculture-related jobs in a region that has long depended on farming.
Article Summary: Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing says it needs 287 million gallons of water a year to cool its proposed 330-megawatt facility. The company had earlier promised not to use Colorado River water because it expected to receive treated wastewater from nearby cities. But after two cities rejected its request, the company is now seeking access to river water.

Article Title: Visa to lay off 7% of its workforce in technology and other teams; CEO Ryan McInerney sends memo saying doing what is right for the company
Article Text:
Visa job cuts to impact 2,600 employees

Visa job cuts to impact technology and product teams

Visa says business remains strong

Visa is planning to cut about 2,600 jobs, or around 7% of its global workforce, as the payments company looks to improve efficiency and invest in future growth opportunities. According to a Bloomberg report, the layoffs will mainly affect employees in the company's technology and product teams, a company spokesperson said. The move comes about six months after rival Mastercard announced job cuts of its own. Visa said AI is helping reshape the way it operates, although the company said AI was not the only reason behind the workforce reduction. The company is expected to report its quarterly earnings after US markets close on Tuesday.Visa said the layoffs will primarily affect employees working in its technology and product divisions. The company’s CEO Ryan McInerney reportedly sent a memo to employees saying:"I have deep conviction that we are doing what is right for Visa, our clients and our partners as we continue to focus on driving efficiency across the company in order to reinvest in our highest potential opportunities”.He added that Visa must continue changing the way it operates to capture growth opportunities and stay ahead of changes in the payments industry, with AI playing an important role in that transformation.“As a result of the choices we have made over the past few years, we are entering a new era in commerce with a business ⁠that has real momentum,” McInerney said in the memo.The layoffs come as more companies adjust their workforces while increasing investments in artificial intelligence.According to the report, AI has helped Visa reduce repetitive tasks and speed up product development, but it was not the only reason behind the decision.Visa employed about 34,100 people in fiscal 2025, up 8% from a year earlier, according to its annual report. The company has exceeded Wall Street's quarterly earnings estimates in all but one quarter over the past two years. Consumer spending also remained strong during the second quarter of 2026, which has supported Visa's business.Analysts at Evercore ISI said they do not see the layoffs as a major concern, describing the move as a way for one of the industry's strongest companies to adjust staffing levels and redirect resources toward higher-growth opportunities, as quoted in the Bloomberg report.
Article Summary: Visa is planning to cut about 2,600 jobs, or around 7% of its global workforce. The layoffs will mainly affect employees in the company's technology and product teams. The company is expected to report its quarterly earnings after US markets close on Tuesday.

Article Title: Europe's most valuable company loses millions after what some analysts say 'nightmare scenario' for ASML due to China's ...
Article Text:
ASML is Europe's most valuable technology company and one of the world's biggest supplier to semiconductor industry

China begins making DUV chipmaking machines

Analysts call it a 'nightmare scenario' for ASML

Shares of ASML, Europe's most valuable technology company, fell sharply on July 28. The stock dropped more than 5% in early trading, wiping billions off the company's market value. The decline came after reports that a Chinese state-backed company has started making deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines, a market long dominated by the Dutch chip equipment maker. While analysts said China's technology still lags behind ASML's, the development is being seen as a potential long-term challenge to the company's strong position in the global semiconductor industry as China continues its push to build advanced chipmaking equipment despite export restrictions.According to previous reports by Reuters and The Information, a Chinese state-backed company has started manufacturing immersion DUV lithography machines. The machines are still at an early stage and do not yet match ASML's technology, the reports said, citing people familiar with the matter.China is expected to produce five DUV machines this year and about 20 next year, far below the roughly 130 comparable machines ASML expects to ship this year.However, the move marks another step in China's efforts to reduce its dependence on foreign chipmaking technology.The reports triggered a sell-off in ASML shares, with the stock falling nearly 6% on Monday, July 27 and dropping more than 5% in early trading on Tuesday, July 28.Some analysts described China's progress as a "nightmare scenario" for ASML because the company dominates the global market for DUV lithography systems, which are widely used to manufacture semiconductors.Despite the latest challenge, demand for ASML's equipment remains strong as the global AI boom drives investment in semiconductor manufacturing. The company recently announced plans to expand production capacity for its EUV machines to meet rising demand from chipmakers.
Article Summary: China begins making DUV chipmaking machines, a market long dominated by ASML. ASML stock dropped more than 5% in early trading, wiping billions off the company's market value. China is expected to produce five DUV machines this year and about 20 next year, far below the roughly 130 comparable machines ASML expects to ship this year.

Article Title: A high school Physics teacher left the Kansas city council meeting on voting for datacenter in handcuffs, dragged out by police after clapping at …
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

What the Emporia Police Department said about the arrest

“On July 22, 2026, the Emporia City Commission held its regularly scheduled meeting. During the course of the meeting, several individuals in attendance were issued verbal warnings by the City Commission regarding disruptive conduct that was interrupting the proceedings.

One individual, Lux Claridge, male, 37years of age, continued this behaviour and was directed to leave the meeting. Claridge did not comply with law enforcement's efforts to remove him from the premises, requiring officers to physically carry him out of the meeting.

Claridge was subsequently arrested and booked into the Lyon County Jail on charges of interference with law enforcement and disorderly conduct.

As with all criminal charges, Claridge is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

The Emporia Police Department remains committed to ensuring public meetings are conducted safely and in an orderly manner, while also respecting the rights of all citizens to participate in the civic process.”

Kansas teacher says arrest will not stop him

“I’m glad to be out, but this is an inconvenience, really. It’s not really deterring me from speaking out or I guess, clapping,”

he said. Claridge has said he plans to plead not guilty when he appears in court in September.

“Seeing them carried out like that was a lot to handle,”

“This isn’t going to hold up in court. Lux is going to fight them on that. I’m looking at avenues to get these people recalled. This is insane to me,”

“Out of all the people that I knew, them getting arrested, I thought someone used a different name or something,”

“We are citizens of this community. We have a right to do our constitutionally-protected activities, which is exactly what they’re violating at this time as well. I think we’re all in a state of fear because of what this government’s doing to us.”

A data centre debate at a city council meeting in Kansas left one resident dealing with legal trouble. Lux Claridge, a 37-year-old Emporia High School physics teacher, was carried out in handcuffs after repeatedly clapping during a public discussion on zoning changes for the proposed Flint Hills Digital Campus data center. This comes after Emporia city’s commissioners had repeatedly warned attendees against disruptive behaviour, including clapping, snapping or making rude comments, before voting on the project.According to the Emporia Police Department, Claridge continued clapping after receiving repeated warnings and was directed to leave the meeting. When he did not comply, officers physically removed him from the chamber before arresting him on charges of interference with law enforcement and disorderly conduct. However, local news outlet KCRG has confirmed that Claridge was released from a Kansas jail after posting bail following his arrest.In its official blog, the Emporia Police Department wrote:Claridge was later released after posting bail and said the arrest would not discourage him from continuing to participate in public meetings, according to the KCRG report.Claridge's wife, Jessica Danford, said that she was present during the meeting and described watching officers remove him.Danford said.Claridge's brother, David Claridge, noted that he believes the charges will not withstand legal scrutiny.he highlighted.Claridge's friend Caleb Rankin also said the arrest surprised him.Rankin added.One community member who attended the meeting also criticised the arrest, saying,Meanwhile, the city commission subsequently approved the zoning changes for the proposed Flint Hills Digital Campus data center after the public meeting.
Article Summary: Lux Claridge, a 37-year-old high school physics teacher, was arrested after repeatedly clapping at a Kansas city council meeting. He was arrested on charges of interference with law enforcement and disorderly conduct. Claridge has said he plans to plead not guilty in court in September.

Article Title: How AI Czar David Sacks 'predicted' what Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said on Chinese open-weights models
Article Text:
David Sacks predicted Anthropic’s messaging shift



“Nobody is trying to ban open source.”

“We just want to limit who can use it.”

“We just want to limit who can contribute to it.”

“We just want to limit how powerful those models can be.”

“We just want to make sure the guardrails (we lobbied for) can’t be removed.”

“The net effect will be the same. They won’t stop until they kneecap open source. The rest of the industry needs to watch these guys like a hawk.”

Anthropic outlines alternative guardrails



Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushed back against industry criticism, insisting that his company has “never advocated for a ban on open-weights models”. The statement comes as tech leaders and former White House AI advisor David Sacks debate whether closed-model AI labs are attempting to restrict open-source technology under the guise of safety.Amodei’s comments have been published in a company blog post following an open letter released late last week by a coalition of major tech companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta and Palantir, urging policymakers to avoid placing “premature restrictions” on open-weight AI models. While chief rival OpenAI eventually added its support to the coalition’s letter, Anthropic declined to sign.The pushback from Amodei is exactly what Sacks posted two days ago (on July 26) with warnings that Anthropic will attempt to “kneecap open source” through targeted lobbying. Sacks said that Anthropic would attempt to reframe its regulatory push to avoid a public backlash while still restricting open-weight developments:“The entire tech industry (save for Anthropic) has come out in favor of open source AI. So what happens next? Will Anthropic change its lobbying efforts? Not likely. Now the gaslighting begins,” he said. Sacks wrote a bunch of points that Anthropic would say on the issue:He said thatIn his blog post, Amodei denied seeking a blanket ban on open-weight software, which allows users to download, modify and run models locally on their own infrastructure. Instead, he argued that national security and safety efforts should focus on hardware access, data scraping and rigorous pre-release evaluations:“To summarize my and Anthropic’s position, we have not and are not advocating for a ban on open-weights models as a category. We should instead focus on keeping powerful chips out of authoritarian hands, stopping industrial-scale distillation, and requiring safety testing of all sufficiently capable models, open and closed,” Amodei wrote.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushed back against industry criticism, insisting that his company has “never advocated for a ban on open-weights models” The statement comes as tech leaders and former White House AI advisor David Sacks debate whether closed-model AI labs are attempting to restrict open-source technology under the guise of safety.

Article Title: Apple launches new leasing program for iPhone, Mac, iPad and Apple Watch in US; partners with Klarna
Article Text:
Apple Upgrade program announced in US

Apple New Upgrade Program offers flexible monthly leasing plans

$17.99 for iPhone

$11.99 for Apple Watch

$24.99 for Mac

$11.99 for iPad

Apple buyers can upgrade, buy or return the device under New Upgrade Program

Apple New Upgrade Program: How to apply

Apple has announced a new leasing program called Apple Upgrade, giving customers in the United States a new way to pay for iPhones, Apple Watches, Macs and iPads through monthly payments. The program is offered in partnership with Klarna and is available through the Apple Store online, the Apple Store app and Apple retail stores. As part of the New Upgrade Program, Apple customers can choose lease plans ranging from 12 to 36 months, trade in eligible devices to lower monthly payments and upgrade to a newer device at the end of the lease. "At Apple, we put the customer at the center of everything we do," said Karen Rasmussen, Apple's vice president of the Apple Store online. "We're thrilled that Apple Upgrade offers our customers, both online and in-store, a more flexible way to pay for the products they love."In the official announcement, Apple said customers can choose 12- or 24-month leasing plans for the iPhone and Apple Watch, while Mac and iPad devices are available with 24- or 36-month lease options.Monthly lease prices start at:Customers can also reduce their monthly payments by trading in an eligible Apple device through Apple Trade In.Those using an Apple Card can earn 3% Daily Cash on lease payments.At the end of the lease period, customers can choose to upgrade to a newer model, buy the device with a one-time payment, or return it and leave the program. Customers can also add an AppleCare subscription to protect their devices during the lease period.With the launch of Apple Upgrade, Apple said it will stop offering the iPhone Upgrade Program and iPhone Payments in the United States. Customers currently enrolled in the iPhone Upgrade Program can switch to Apple Upgrade when eligible, continue with Apple Card Monthly Installments, purchase a device outright or use carrier financing.Apple said customers can apply for the leasing program online or in stores and receive a decision from Klarna within minutes. The company said all applicants will undergo a soft credit check, which does not affect their credit score.Once approved, customers can complete their purchase as usual. In-store buyers can take their device home immediately, while online customers can choose home delivery or store pickup. Apple also said customers will continue to have access to Personal Setup services and free Today at Apple sessions to help them learn how to use their devices.
Article Summary: Apple has announced a new leasing program called Apple Upgrade. The program gives customers a new way to pay for iPhones, Apple Watches, Macs and iPads. Apple customers can choose lease plans ranging from 12 to 36 months. At the end of the lease period, customers can upgrade to a newer model.

Article Title: How OpenAI and Anthropic are on track to beat these 50-year-old-plus American brands
Article Text:
Anthropic accounts for around 60% of the combined revenue estimate of Starbucks and McDonald's

Anthropic revenue estimate tops Starbucks and McDonald's combined

Young AI companies challenge long-established businesses

AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic are growing so quickly that they are on track to generate more annual revenue than some of America's biggest and oldest consumer brands, per an Axios report. The two AI firms are expected to reach a combined annual revenue run rate of around $120 billion, according to data from AI investment research platform Funda, cited by Key Context author Tae Kim. If that happens, both companies would rank among the top 100 companies in the Fortune 500 by revenue, it added. The figures highlight the rapid growth of the AI industry and show why companies continue to invest billions of dollars in AI infrastructure and services.According to the report, Anthropic accounts for around 60% of the combined revenue estimate because of its strong business with enterprise customers. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI is working to close that gap. The Claude-maker is estimated to reach an annual revenue run rate of about $71 billion. At that level, the AI startup would generate more revenue than Starbucks and McDonald's combined. Starbucks reported $37.2 billion in annual revenue, while McDonald's generated $26.9 billion.Anthropic's projected revenue would also come close to surpassing the combined revenue of Starbucks, McDonald's and Yum Brands, the parent company of Taco Bell and KFC.The comparison highlights how quickly AI companies are expanding. Starbucks, McDonald's, Taco Bell and KFC are global brands that have been around for 50 to more than 100 years. Together, they operate tens of thousands of restaurants worldwide and are among the best-known consumer brands.Anthropic, by comparison, was founded only five years ago. The report said the strong revenue growth of OpenAI and Anthropic also helps explain why technology companies continue to spend heavily on AI infrastructure, with industry forecasts calling for trillions of dollars in AI-related investments over the coming years.
Article Summary: Anthropic accounts for around 60% of the combined revenue estimate of Starbucks and McDonald's. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI is estimated to reach an annual revenue run rate of about $71 billion. Both companies would rank among the top 100 companies in the Fortune 500 by revenue.

Article Title: IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw says India’s space rockets will soon get homegrown chips
Article Text:
"Made in Bharat" chips for space rockets soon, says Ashwini Vaishnaw

Private space flight milestones drive hardware integration

Prime Minister Modi praises private space sector progress

India will soon power its domestic space rockets with homegrown semiconductors, union minister for electronics and information technology, Ashwini Vaishnaw , has said. The announcement follows a meeting between Vaishnaw and the leadership of private space technology firm Skyroot Aerospace, coming on the heels of the successful orbital launch of their Vikram-1 rocket.Taking to social media platform X, Vaishnaw shared his optimism for domestic tech integration, writing: “'Made in Bharat' chips for our rockets... soon!”The push for domestic hardware integration comes as India’s private space industry achieves major operational milestones, as per a report by ANI. On July 18, Skyroot Aerospace launched the Vikram-1 Test Flight-1, successfully injecting its payloads into a 450-kilometre orbit. The mission marked the maiden flight of India’s first privately developed orbital-class rocket and made India only the third country in the world with private orbital launch capabilities, ANI added.Acknowledging Vaishnaw's post, Skyroot Aerospace reaffirmed its commitment to integrating Indian-made hardware into its launch vehicles:“Honoured to meet Hon'ble Union Minister Shri @AshwiniVaishnaw. India's deep-tech ecosystem is accelerating – powered by forward-looking reforms, world-class digital infrastructure, and a strong commitment to innovation...We look forward to the day India-built chips fly on our rockets,” the company wrote on X (formerly Twitter).The minister’s announcement follows a high-level meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Skyroot Aerospace co-founders Pawan Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka. In a post on X, Modi commended the founders’ vision, noting that the success of Vikram-1 featured prominently in their conversation.“A great interaction with Pawan Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka of Skyroot Aerospace. Their energy, ambition and positivity reflect the vibrant spirit of our private space ecosystem. Best wishes to the entire Skyroot team,” Modi wrote.
Article Summary: India will soon power its domestic space rockets with homegrown semiconductors, union minister for electronics and information technology, Ashwini Vaishnaw has said. The announcement follows a meeting between Vaishesnaw and the leadership of private space technology firm Skyroot Aerospace.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Elon Musk: "It's OK to have your eggs in one basket as long as..."
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Elon Musk

"It's OK to have your eggs in one basket as long as you control what happens to that basket"

What does this quote mean?

Focus often achieves more than distraction

Control reduces uncertainty

Commitment builds confidence and expertise

Risk should be calculated, not avoided

Why this quote still matters today

Conventional wisdom often tells us, "Don't put all your eggs in one basket." Diversifying our efforts is generally seen as the safest path. Yet entrepreneur Elon Musk offers a different perspective: "It's OK to have your eggs in one basket as long as you control what happens to that basket." Rather than discouraging commitment, the quote argues that success often comes from focusing intensely on one important goal while maintaining control over the factors that determine its outcome. It reminds us that taking calculated risks is not reckless when it is supported by preparation, knowledge and responsibility.Elon Musk, a businessman and entrepreneur known for leading companies such as Tesla, SpaceX, Neuralink and xAI. Throughout his career, he has often pursued ambitious ideas by concentrating significant time, money and effort on a small number of long-term goals, demonstrating the importance of conviction and strategic decision-making.The quote teaches that concentrating your resources on a single goal can be a wise strategy if you have enough knowledge, preparation and influence over the outcome.Success is not simply about avoiding risk, it is about understanding it, managing it and taking responsibility for the decisions you make. Rather than spreading yourself too thin, the saying encourages focused effort backed by careful planning. Its enduring message is that commitment, combined with control and disciplined execution, often achieves more than dividing your attention across too many competing priorities.Many people divide their time among too many projects, hoping that one will eventually succeed. While diversification has its place, constantly switching between priorities can prevent meaningful progress. Musk's words suggest that deep commitment to one important objective often produces better results than giving limited attention to many. Extraordinary achievements usually require sustained focus rather than scattered effort.The key idea in the quote is not putting everything into one basket, it is controlling the basket. Before making a major investment, launching a business or pursuing a challenging career, successful people work to understand the risks, gather information and prepare for setbacks. The more control you have through planning, expertise and adaptability, the less your success depends on luck alone.When people dedicate themselves fully to a meaningful goal, they develop skills, experience and confidence that would be difficult to gain through half-hearted effort. Every challenge overcome strengthens their ability to handle the next one. Whether learning a profession, building a company or mastering a craft, wholehearted commitment often becomes the foundation of long-term success.Musk's quote does not encourage blind optimism or reckless decisions. Instead, it highlights the importance of taking calculated risks, those supported by research, preparation and a clear understanding of the possible outcomes. Every successful entrepreneur, scientist or leader has faced uncertainty, but the most effective ones minimise unnecessary risks while maximising their ability to influence the result. Courage is most powerful when paired with careful planning.In a world filled with endless opportunities and constant distractions, it is easy to lose focus by trying to do everything at once. Musk's message reminds us that lasting success often comes from identifying what matters most and committing to it wholeheartedly while remaining responsible for the decisions we make. The enduring lesson behind this quote is simple: focus your efforts, understand the risks, take ownership of the outcome and never leave your future entirely to chance.
Article Summary: "It's OK to have your eggs in one basket as long as you control what happens to that basket" Elon Musk, a businessman and entrepreneur known for leading companies such as Tesla, SpaceX, Neuralink and xAI. The key idea in the quote is not putting everything into one basket, it is controlling the basket.

Article Title: US-China chip smuggling tensions reach Taiwan; Nvidia offices searched, employee detained
Article Text:
Nvidia employee detained after home and office searches

Taiwanese prosecutors have detained an Nvidia employee and searched the company's offices as part of an expanding investigation into the alleged smuggling of AI chips to China, reported Bloomberg citing people familiar with the matter. The case is linked to an ongoing probe into suspected exports of Nvidia's AI accelerators in violation of US trade restrictions. As per the report, the latest action is believed to be the first known case of Taiwanese authorities taking legal action against an Nvidia employee as they widen their investigation into the suspected illegal movement of advanced AI hardware.According to the report, Taiwanese investigators also searched the employee's home and his desk at Nvidia's Taipei office on July 24. The officials later asked a court for permission to detain the employee on allegations of forgery and breach of trust. The court approved the request, people cited in the report said.The identity of the employee has not been made public.Taiwan authorities previously detain three people suspecting Nvidia chips getting smuggled to China via JapanThe investigation follows an earlier round of detentions carried out by Taiwanese authorities in May.A previous Bloomberg report said that the Taiwan prosecutors suspect that three individuals successfully smuggled at least one shipment of Nvidia AI chips to China after first exporting them to Japan.The authorities then detained three people, including employees linked to Super Micro Computer Inc., an AI server reseller and a data centre operator, were accused of falsifying documents to export Nvidia AI chips to China despite US export restrictions.As part of their investigation, Taiwanese authorities are investigating whether advanced Nvidia AI accelerators were illegally shipped to China through other countries.
Article Summary: Taiwanese prosecutors have detained an Nvidia employee on allegations of forgery and breach of trust. Investigators also searched the employee's home and his desk at Nvidia's Taipei office on July 24. The case is linked to an ongoing probe into suspected exports of Nvidia's AI accelerators in violation of US trade restrictions.

Article Title: Some of the biggest names in AI and tech industry have donated over $65 million on midterm elections to shape balance of power on issues related to ban on datacenters, AI regulation and more
Article Text:
AI image for representative purpose

Silicon Valley heavyweights back pro-AI super PAC network



$50 million from venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.

$25 million from OpenAI President Greg Brockman and his wife, Anna.

$25 million combined from Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz ($12.5 million each).

$500,000 from SV Angel Founder Ron Conway.

Anthropic and former lawmakers counter with safety-first coalition



Meta focuses millions on state legislatures



Silicon Valley’s top executives and AI startups are donating large sums of money for the upcoming midterm elections, a report has said, adding that this mounts a proxy war to shape the next Congress and key state legislatures. As per The Financial Times, networks of super PACs linked to tech giants like OpenAI , Anthropic, Meta and venture capital heavyweights have already spent more than $65 million.Their goal is simple: steer federal and local policy on critical issues that range from state-level data centre bans to strict oversight of advanced AI models, the report said. The massive spending surge comes at a time when the public adoption of AI tools is at an all-time high and political scrutiny has intensified.Where local opposition is mounting against the energy demands of massive data centers, federal regulators grapple with safety standards and competition from Chinese open-weight models like Moonshot AI’s recently-launched Kimi K3.Leading the campaign against heavy regulation is Leading the Future, a pro-AI super PAC network backed by prominent tech investors and executives. The group’s main umbrella PAC raised nearly $76 million by the end of June, the report noted., adding that the key contributions include:OpenAI has clarified that Brockman’s contributions were made in a personal capacity.The publication says that to influence both sides of the aisle, Leading the Future redirected funds into two targeted super PACs: Think Big (focused on Democratic primaries) and American Mission (focused on Republican races). Together, the two branches have spent over $29 million.Think Big notably spent $8 million in New York's 12th Congressional District primary against Assemblyman Alex Bores, an advocate for strict AI regulation. Meanwhile, American Mission has spent $10.7 million supporting 19 Republican congressional candidates nationwide.In response to the pro-industry push, a rival political network called Public First Action has emerged to back candidates advocating for strict AI safety standards. Co-founded by former congressmen Chris Stewart (R-UT) and Brad Carson (D-OK), the network boasts an $80 million war chest.AI startup Anthropic supplied $40 million to the group. Anthropic noted that its increased giving was spurred by rapid technological leaps, including its advanced Claude Mythos model. Additional backing came from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei ($1 million) and Alignment Science lead Jan Leike ($500,000 total).Public First Action operates through allied groups, including the Jobs and Democracy PAC (Democratic focus) and Defending Our Values PAC (GOP focus). Jobs and Democracy PAC spent over $15 million in New York to counter Leading the Future’s efforts and support pro-regulation candidates.While rival networks clash over federal policy, Meta is reportedly directing its political spending toward state-level races to prevent a fragmented landscape of local AI laws. The parent company of WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook donated $20 million to Mobilizing Economic Transformation Across (Meta) California to influence state legislative races in its home state, spending $1.3 million to boost Democratic state Senate candidate Scott Sakakihara.For races outside California, Meta contributed $45 million to the American Technology Excellence Project, a 527 organisation.
Article Summary: Silicon Valley’s top executives and AI startups are donating large sums of money for the upcoming midterm elections. Networks of super PACs linked to tech giants like OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and venture capital heavyweights have already spent more than $65 million. Their goal is to steer federal and local policy on critical issues that range from state-level data centre bans to strict oversight of advanced AI models.

Article Title: Microsoft executives are asking why CEO Satya Nadella is feeding rivals' products before his own
Article Text:
Microsoft executives are asking why CEO Satya Nadella is feeding rivals' products before his own

Microsoft CFO Amy Hood put Azure customers last in the GPU queue, and the stock fell 10% the same week

Microsoft's $190 billion AI capex has it renting compute from Amazon and Google after GitHub outages

'All of the supply is gone': why Microsoft executives say frontier labs and Adobe come before M365 Copilot

Three years ago Satya Nadella was the man who started the AI race. In February 2023 he stood in front of a packed audience outside Seattle, unveiled an AI-powered Bing, and told Google the fight was on. CNN Business made him CEO of the Year. One former Microsoft executive told Business Insider he was "like a superhero" back then.The scoreboard reads differently now. Microsoft's stock is down more than 24% from a year ago, the worst showing in the Magnificent 7. Copilot trails ChatGPT and Claude. Xbox's boss has called the business "not healthy". And inside the company, according to Business Insider's reporting, executives are openly questioning where the compute from a record $190 billion capital spending year is actually going—because a lot of it is not going to Microsoft's own products.On the January earnings call, CFO Amy Hood laid out Microsoft's allocation order without much diplomacy. First-party apps first: sales usage, M365 Copilot, GitHub Copilot. Then long-term R&D and product innovation. Whatever survives that goes to Azure customers.Hood offered a number to soften it. Had those GPUs gone to Azure instead of Microsoft's own AI products in the first half of the fiscal year, Azure growth would have hit just over 40% rather than 39%.Investors weren't soothed. The stock fell more than 10% after that report, with the slower Azure outlook landing badly against record AI spending.Executives told Business Insider the tradeoffs have only sharpened since. Demand for infrastructure is outrunning Microsoft's ability to build it, and $190 billion in capex has not closed the gap.The workarounds are telling. After a run of GitHub outages this year, Amazon stepped in to help. Microsoft looked at leasing Oracle infrastructure and walked away over security and compliance concerns. It is now evaluating Amazon and Google for more capacity. "We are shopping for capacity everywhere," one person familiar with the talks said.Meanwhile the Azure sales team is being asked to sell more of a product Microsoft is struggling to supply. Some quotas have gone up by 30% this year.The internal frustration is specific. "All of the supply is gone once you solve for frontier labs and our internal businesses like M365 and Microsoft AI," one executive told Business Insider.Another put it more bluntly, asking why Nadella would prioritise growing Adobe over growing M365—Adobe being an Azure tenant burning capacity that Microsoft's own productivity suite could use. "I have no idea how we're going to land that message with customers," the person said.That tension sits on top of a company already being reshaped. Nadella promoted Judson Althoff to run the commercial business, retired the traditional senior leadership team structure, and watched Rajesh Jha retire and Yusuf Mehdi prepare to leave. The performance review system has been overhauled into five sharper categories, which executives say feels like a return to Ballmer-era stack ranking. "It's almost like the old era of Microsoft is back," one former executive said. "The old Windows era where you lead with a lot of fear and a billy club in your hand."Microsoft’s fourth-quarter results will show whether the spending is working. The internal question is simpler: who is it working for.
Article Summary: Microsoft CFO Amy Hood put Azure customers last in the GPU queue. Microsoft's $190 billion AI capex has it renting compute from Amazon and Google after GitHub outages. "All of the supply is gone once you solve for frontier labs and our internal businesses like M365 and Microsoft AI," one executive said.

Article Title: T-Mobile outage: Company says service restored, read full statement
Article Text:
What is ‘SOS’ or ‘SOS only’ means



T-Mobile has said that it has fully restored network service after a widespread outage that left tens of thousands of US customers without cellular signal or mobile internet. The disruption began around 4:00 p.m. ET on July 27, causing reports to surge on tracking platform Downdetector. At its peak, more than 62,000 incidents were logged nationwide, with users across several states, including California, Georgia, Arizona and Utah, reporting that their phones were stuck in “SOS” mode.“We have fully restored service for all customers and sincerely apologize for the difficulties to those who experienced network impacts today,” the wireless carrier said in a post on X (formerly Twitter), adding, “At @TMobile, we know that customers rely on us to stay connected to what matters most, and we appreciate their understanding as we prioritised resolution.”Users complained that their phones displayed “SOS” or “SOS only”. This means that the device has lost connection to its primary cellular network, though emergency calls can still be placed. During the peak of the disruption, T-Mobile acknowledged the issue and stated that resolving the technical challenges was its highest priority:“Our teams are actively working on the reports of technical challenges impacting some customers.Any service impacts are in the process of being resolved and are our highest priority. We know how critical it is to stay connected and every available resource is focused on resolving this as quickly as possible,” the company said in a statement on X. T-Mobile did not immediately provide a specific cause for the technical glitch.According to Downdetector data, the majority of user-submitted complaints focused on mobile phone connections, complete loss of signal and failing mobile internet access.Minor spikes in outage reports were also noted by users of other major networks during the same timeframe, including around 1,000 reports for Verizon and 850 for AT&T, which often occurs when subscribers attempt to place cross-network calls to an affected provider.
Article Summary: T-Mobile has said that it has fully restored network service after a widespread outage. The disruption began around 4:00 p.m. ET on July 27, causing reports to surge on tracking platform Downdetector. At its peak, more than 62,000 incidents were logged nationwide.

Article Title: Cursor launches Rs 649 India-only ‘Start’ plan: What you get, and what stays locked
Article Text:
Cursor Start lands in India at Rs 649 a month, with UPI payments and Grok 4.5 access

Cursor Start plan includes Grok 4.5 , Composer and cloud agents for Rs 649, but no OpenAI or Anthropic models

Why Cursor picked India for its first localised pricing

AI coding startup Cursor has launched its first country-specific subscription, and India is the test case. Cursor Start costs Rs 649 a month, tax inclusive, and slots in between the company's free tier and its $20 Pro plan. It went live this week, just weeks before SpaceX is expected to close its $60 billion all-stock acquisition of the startup.The pricing isn't charity. India is already Cursor's third-largest market, with a user base that tripled over the past year to more than 3 million developers. The company says Indian users run more agent requests per developer than anyone else in the world. Payments go through UPI, credit or debit card, which was the second thing Indian users had been asking for.Start includes Grok 4.5, Cursor's most powerful in-house model, and Composer, its cheaper coding model. You also get always-on cloud agents that build and open pull requests while you work elsewhere, the Cursor iOS app, and support for plugins, MCP servers, hooks and skills. Agent limits sit well above the free plan across desktop, web, iOS and CLI.The gaps matter just as much. Start does not include frontier models from OpenAI or Anthropic.Bugbot, Auto mode, Automations and the Cursor SDK all stay behind Pro, along with on-demand usage past the included limits. Simon Green, Cursor's head of Asia-Pacific and Japan, told TechCrunch the company saw a chance to "right-size the commercial model and drive scale". Cursor will also run checks to stop people outside India from signing up through VPNs.The talent math explains the choice. GitHub counted more than 27 million Indian developers on its platform this year, second only to the US, with over two million joining in 2026 alone. OpenAI and Anthropic have both rolled out India-specific plans over the past year.Green said the plan is commercially sustainable rather than a loss leader, because it runs on Cursor's own models. Other markets could follow if it works, much like OpenAI did with ChatGPT Go. Cursor is hiring locally too: a first India salesperson, a leader in Delhi, a government affairs office and three technical support roles across Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad and Mumbai. Once the SpaceX deal closes in Q3, Green said Starlink's existing India footprint could help Cursor scale faster.
Article Summary: Cursor Start plan includes Grok 4.5, Composer and cloud agents for Rs 649, but no OpenAI or Anthropic models. Payments go through UPI, credit or debit card. India is already Cursor's third-largest market, with a user base that tripled over the past year to more than 3 million developers.

Article Title: As iPhone 18 series launch nears, the price of staying loyal to Apple is rising
Article Text:
Apple is expected to bring iPhone 18 series later this year in September

Apple premium is getting pricier

iPhone is an outlier, but may not be for long

Every Apple user eventually gets an offer they can't refuse: buy another Apple product. An iPhone leads to AirPods, which leads to a Mac, then an Apple Watch, iCloud, Apple Music and AppleCare+. The ecosystem has always been designed to pull users deeper in. Now it's asking them to pay more at every step. There was a time when buying into the Apple ecosystem meant paying a premium once and then enjoying the benefits of seamless integration across devices and services. That premium was never small, but it was relatively predictable.That equation is changing. Over the past month, Apple has quietly raised prices across almost every part of its ecosystem — hardware, extended warranties and subscription services. Some increases are being blamed on soaring memory prices, others on higher music licensing costs, while currency movements have driven hikes in markets such as Japan. The reasons differ, but the outcome is the same: staying inside Apple's ecosystem is becoming steadily more expensive.The June hardware price increases were the biggest signal. Macs and iPads saw sharp revisions after Apple cited unprecedented increases in DRAM and NAND flash memory costs.The company said the explosion of AI infrastructure globally has created intense demand for high-bandwidth memory, squeezing supply and raising component prices. The impact was significant.The MacBook Air, long considered Apple's most accessible premium laptop, now starts at Rs 1,49,900 instead of Rs 1,19,900. The 15-inch model moved to Rs 1,79,900. The entry-level iPad climbed to Rs 44,900, while the iPad Air and iPad Pro also became substantially costlier. Even refurbished products, traditionally Apple's value proposition for budget-conscious buyers, are no longer insulated from these increases.The ripple effect is visible beyond computers and tablets. AppleCare+ subscriptions for Macs and iPads now cost more. Existing subscribers have been protected, but anyone buying a new device will pay higher monthly or annual charges simply to insure it. Then came services.Apple Music now costs more, with Apple explicitly pointing to rising licensing costs. Apple One Family and Premier bundles have also become more expensive. Individually, these increases appear modest. Collectively, they raise the cost of remaining fully invested in Apple's ecosystem.This is where Apple's pricing strategy becomes interesting. Unlike many consumer electronics companies that depend largely on one-time hardware sales, Apple increasingly earns recurring revenue from services. Hardware brings customers into the ecosystem; subscriptions keep them there.Apple's ecosystem has always worked like a beautifully designed trap. You don't notice it closing until you're already inside. By then, your photos are in iCloud, your music is on Apple Music, you can’t go a day without checking those three rings on the Watch, and your AirPods jump between devices with so much ease that you never, ever think about any other wireless earbuds.Higher recurring fees therefore have an outsized impact. A customer who buys a Mac, an iPhone and an iPad is no longer paying only for devices. They are paying every month for storage, entertainment, warranties and bundled services. Even Apple's accessories illustrate the growing premium.The AirPods Max, ridiculously priced at Rs 67,900, remain among the most expensive mainstream wireless headphones despite increasing competition from Sony, Bose and Sennheiser . Their appeal lies less in audio quality alone than in how effortlessly they integrate with iPhones, Macs and iPads through automatic device switching, spatial audio and Apple's broader ecosystem. That convenience, however, now carries an increasingly steep price tag. For many consumers, the biggest question is what happens nextThe iPhone has so far escaped a global price increase, although Japan recently saw prices rise by up to 11%. That move was largely attributed to currency fluctuations, but it also shows Apple is willing to recalibrate prices market by market when conditions demand it. The more significant test will come later this year.Industry watchers increasingly expect Apple's next iPhone lineup to launch at higher prices as elevated component costs continue to pressure margins. Unlike memory shortages of previous cycles, today's constraints are closely linked to AI infrastructure spending, suggesting they may persist for longer.If iPhone prices rise, the psychological impact could be considerable. The smartphone remains the anchor product around which Apple's ecosystem revolves. A higher entry price could also make upgrading less frequent, pushing more consumers towards financing schemes, trade-in programmes and certified refurbished devices.Then there is the foldable iPhone. Whenever Apple launches its first foldable device (expected in September), it is unlikely to compete on affordability. Given the cost of foldable displays, complex hinge mechanisms and Apple's traditional premium positioning, the device could comfortably become the most expensive iPhone the company has ever sold in India, potentially redefining the upper end of the smartphone market.None of this appears accidental. Apple has spent years transforming itself from a hardware company into an ecosystem company. Once customers own multiple Apple devices, subscribe to several services and rely on ecosystem-specific features, price sensitivity naturally declines. That gives Apple more room than most competitors to pass on higher costs without dramatically affecting loyalty.Whether that strategy continues to work depends on how much consumers value integration over affordability. Apple continues to offer one of the most polished technology ecosystems available. But as hardware, services, warranties and accessories all move higher together, the cost of belonging is climbing faster than ever.The Apple ecosystem still delivers convenience. The question is whether that convenience is becoming a luxury that fewer consumers are willing to keep paying for.
Article Summary: Apple has quietly raised prices across almost every part of its ecosystem. Some increases are being blamed on soaring memory prices, others on higher music licensing costs, while currency movements have driven hikes in markets such as Japan. AppleCare+ subscriptions for Macs and iPads now cost more.

Article Title: 'Mid-2030s at the earliest': Analysts wrote off China's chipmaking ambitions, now the first homegrown machines ship this year
Article Text:
SMIC, Hua Hong and CXMT get China's first domestic DUV tools this year (Picture Credits: AP)

Why immersion DUV matters more to China than any other chipmaking tool

Five machines in 2026, 20 in 2027: what the numbers actually tell you

A state-backed company in Shanghai has started mass-producing immersion deep ultraviolet lithography machines, the chipmaking tool that ASML has effectively owned for two decades. The first units are due this year at SMIC, Hua Hong Semiconductor and memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies, according to The Information, which cited two people familiar with the programme. None of them would name the manufacturer.The timing is what stings. In June, the AI Futures Project put commercial-scale Chinese immersion DUV somewhere in the mid-2030s, with ASML sitting on 98.7% of the market. That forecast is barely a month old. ASML shares fell more than 7% on Monday, the stock's worst day since June 8, and the selling spread down the supply chain: BE Semiconductor dropped about 8.5%, Soitec 5%, Infineon nearly 3%.Immersion DUV is the ceiling for Chinese fabs. EUV is off the table under export controls, so these machines are the most advanced lithography Chinese chipmakers can legally touch. They print 28nm-class features in a single exposure and can be pushed to 7nm through multipatterning, which costs yield and stacks up overlay errors, but works.SMIC's third-generation 7nm node was built this way.The new systems are mostly domestic, though some critical parts still come from Japan. Development teams were pulled together from several Chinese firms, one of them the state-backed startup Shanghai Yuliangsheng Technology, whose immersion tool SMIC has been testing since September 2025. Supplier delays have capped output this year.Volume is the reality check. Roughly five machines this year and about 20 in 2027, against the 130 immersion systems ASML expects to ship in 2026. CFO Roger Dassen told analysts in July that ASML plans to raise immersion capacity by 30% in 2027 and is looking at another 30% for 2028. The domestic tools also trail on performance, reliability and build quality, and qualifying any of them on a live production line can take months.There is a policy angle too. US House Resolution 8170 would name SMIC, Hua Hong, CXMT, Huawei and YMTC as restricted entities in law, cutting them off from ASML sales and servicing. Three of those five are the first customers for the Chinese scanner. The MATCH Act, introduced in April and reported out of committee on 22 April, covers servicing and technical assistance, not just new exports, which would reach the ASML tools already installed inside Chinese fabs.China is separately working on a domestic EUV machine. That one is still a prototype.
Article Summary: State-backed company in Shanghai has started mass-producing immersion deep ultraviolet lithography machines. The first units are due this year at SMIC, Hua Hong Semiconductor and memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies. ASML shares fell more than 7% on Monday, the stock's worst day since June 8.

Article Title: Bruce Blakeman warns New York governor Kathy Hochul: You are forcing family farms, small businesses and family homes to be sold, New Yorkers are being punished for building future for their kids and g
Article Text:
Warning on passing wealth to future generations



Kathy Hochul’s Pied-à-Terre tax



Economic divide and business pushback



Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, the Republican challenger to New York Gov. Kathy Hochul has accused the governor and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani of pushing tax policies that could force families to sell homes, farms, or small businesses to cover inheritance-related bills. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Blakeman said: “Family farms, small businesses, and family homes shouldn’t have to be sold just to pay another tax.”In an accompanying video, Blakeman argued that New Yorkers who spend their lives building equity in property or businesses are being punished when trying to pass those assets to their children and grandchildren. “When you die, your family farm, your family business, or your family home will have to be sold to be able to pay the tax. That’s just wrong. When I become governor, I will stop it,” he said.Blakeman’s criticism comes as Hochul and Mamdani back higher taxes on wealthy property owners, including New York’s new pied-à-terre tax. The measure applies to non-primary residences valued at $5 million or more and is projected to generate $500 million annually for the city. Hochul has defended the tax, saying owners of “ultra-luxury second homes” should contribute more.The tax has already drawn resistance from wealthy property owners. Citadel founder Ken Griffin warned about investment shifting to lower-tax markets and threatened to reconsider a $6 billion redevelopment project in New York. Griffin has argued that businesses are paying high taxes without receiving adequate services in return, pointing to Citadel’s expansion in Miami as evidence of the state’s competitive disadvantage.Blakeman and Hochul have also clashed over economic policy beyond taxes. Blakeman opposed Hochul’s decision to pause approvals for large data centers consuming 50 megawatts or more, arguing that local governments should decide whether projects move forward based on economic benefits.
Article Summary: Bruce Blakeman, the Republican challenger to New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, has accused the governor and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani of pushing tax policies that could force families to sell homes, farms, or small businesses to cover inheritance-related bills. “Family farms, small businesses, and family homes shouldn’t have to be sold just to pay another tax,” he said.

Article Title: Microsoft unveils Project Perception and MAI-Cyber-1-Flash; claims new cybersecurity AI model beats Gemini and GPT on vulnerability detection while cutting costs by 50%
Article Text:
Project Perception brings AI agents together for cyber defence

Red agents, which identify potential attack paths and software vulnerabilities before they are exploited.

Blue agents which investigate findings, analyse security context and determine which risks require attention.

New Cyber Stack built around AI

"The physics of cybersecurity are changing. Autonomous systems can now reason, adapt and operate continuously. At the same time, the cost of offence is falling, while the volume, velocity and complexity of what must be secured continues to grow."
